lens: Voice-first ambient: full-screen FaceTime-like call, orb-centric, chrome disappears during the call
name: Ambient Orb Call Room
one_liner: A FaceTime-style call room: a breathing orb carries the conversation, the chrome fades mid-call, and live rubric arcs and whisper cues appear only when they matter.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the voice-first ambient lens for the live call and carried the orb across the whole product as the brand mark, persona avatar and debrief header. Research shaped three choices. Mobbin's Delphi call screen (centered avatar, status pill, two call controls) validated the minimal-chrome call. Second Nature and Hyperbound both lead with video-avatar or chrome-heavy practice, so a voice-first orb is a real differentiator. Descript's side co-pilot pattern fits the wizard better than a long form. Text mode keeps the same canvas with a smaller orb, so the brief's text simulation is not lost.

design_language.typography: Instrument Sans for UI at 400 to 600 (body 15/24). Instrument Serif italic for whisper cues, the landing hero (64px) and the debrief verdict. Geist Mono with tabular numerals for timers and scores. All three are open-license Google Fonts; Inter and Sora are retired.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 20px card radius, 28px call-room panels, full pills for chips and status. Dark mode uses 1px line borders and a faint top highlight instead of shadows. Only the floating whisper card uses backdrop blur (16px, 8% white). The orb is the single source of glow.
design_language.motion: Idle orb breathes on a 4s cycle and scales from 0.96 to 1.08 with the speaker's audio level. Chrome fades to 0 after 3s without pointer or touch, at 250ms ease-out. Whisper cards rise in 300ms and dwell 6s. Halo arcs tween over 600ms when criteria change. With prefers-reduced-motion, the orb freezes to a static gradient and transitions become opacity-only.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75 stroke: 20px in rails, 24px in call controls. No emoji in the UI. The logo is the orb glyph, a circle with one arc that doubles as the rubric halo.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark is the default for landing, pre-call and the call room. Light leads for library, wizard, debrief and dashboard. Respects prefers-color-scheme with a visible toggle. Both modes are token-driven, so the orb and halo recolor without per-component overrides.

navigation_and_ia: Five destinations: Practice, Library, Create (wizard), Progress, and Team (shown only to org members with a manager role). Desktop uses a 64px left rail with icons and hover labels; it collapses during a call. Mobile uses a bottom tab bar with four tabs plus More. Cmd-K opens the library and wizard from anywhere. During a live call the rail and tab bar disappear, leaving only the orb, timer and controls. Pre-call and debrief remain linked from the Practice tab so nothing is lost.

An objection turns the halo coral and adds a one-line pivot card. The bottom rail (mute, text, talk-track dots, End and grade) appears on movement; the transcript sits in a drag-up sheet.

Mute and End and grade are 64px circles in the thumb zone; a grab handle at the bottom opens the transcript and talk-track sheet (Vaul). Only the timer remains in the top bar, and safe-area insets are respected. Text mode collapses the orb into a 96px header with chat below.

live_coaching_and_scoring: A separate coach channel reads the rolling transcript after every rep turn and returns structured JSON: a whisper cue, an objection type, criterion coverage deltas and a talk-track step. The persona never receives coach output, so the persona still cannot coach. Target latency is a cue within about 1.5s of the persona finishing; the default model is gpt-4.1-mini, selectable in settings. Live scores render as a dashed halo labelled live estimate. The full grader, with quotes, replaces it with a solid halo at End and grade. Without an API key, the existing keyword heuristic drives the same halo and shows a heuristic chip. Optional audio whisper: a second Realtime session audible only to the rep, for headphone users.
persona_library_and_wizard: The library ships as versioned persona packs in the repo, one YAML file per persona: role, seniority, industry, temperament, objections, difficulty, voice id and rubric preset. A zod schema validates every file in CI. The seed target is 120 personas across 14 jobs: SDR cold call, AE discovery, CS renewal, collections, solar, home services, insurance, mortgage, real estate, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting and retail. The wizard runs in four steps: ingest (paste, URL fetch, CRM notes or transcript), a structured-output draft of persona plus rubric, a duplicate check against the nearest library entry, and a test call. Users can save locally or export a PR-ready file to contribute upstream.
signature_moments: The halo: five rubric arcs fill live around the orb as each criterion is covered.
Chrome dissolves after 3 seconds, leaving only the orb, timer and one whisper.
Whisper cues appear in Instrument Serif italic, are read once, then fade.
The wizard fills a persona card field by field, each field carrying a source chip back to the pasted text.
Debrief moments timeline: click a score jump and replay those 30 seconds.
Library sections per sales job with View all (n), so the 14 jobs read like a catalogue.
openai_fund_angle: Show the OpenAI stack instead of hiding it. Each screen carries a model provenance line: persona voice (ElevenLabs today, with OpenAI Realtime added as a selectable engine), coach (gpt-4.1-mini), grader (gpt-4.1-mini default, gpt-4.1 selectable), wizard (Structured Outputs). Settings shows estimated cost per call. The repo gets a How this repo uses Codex page covering PR review, maintainer automation and release workflows, the uses the Codex for Open Source program names; the Codex Open Source Fund offers grants up to $25K in API credits. Contributors get a Contribute a persona PR template, good-first-persona labels and a contributor wall. Selection is at OpenAI's discretion, so the page should show real usage rather than promise it.

inspirations.borrowed: The real-call-to-practice loop as the gap to close: scenario categories such as gatekeeper, voicemail and renewal. Vendor-authored.
Program scope: API credits for projects using Codex in PR review, maintainer automation and release workflows; the repo must demonstrate these uses.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1 (1-2 weeks): move tokens to CSS variables and add shadcn primitives on existing routes, keeping URLs. Phase 2: the call room with orb, halo and coach channel behind a feature flag, with text mode kept. Phase 3: persona seeds, facet library and wizard. Phase 4: debrief timeline, progress dashboard and team lanes. Each phase ships to the live Vercel demo and the README is updated per phase.

risks: Scorecard (proposer self-score; 1-10, with 5 = baseline for D and E): A look 8, B UX 7, C unique 8, D live coaching 5.4, E library and wizard 5.6, F1 SaaS 6, F2 selling to entities 6, F3 not worth it 3 (worth building).
Chrome-fade can hide controls and evidence; mitigate by never fading focused controls and by a hold-to-reveal transcript sheet.
Coach latency and per-turn cost; throttle to rep turns and cache identical transcript windows.
WebGL orb on low-end phones; fall back to a CSS radial gradient carrying the same halo.
Dark-first can read as generic AI; the orb and halo must carry identity, so the light theme needs equal polish.
120 seeded personas is content-heavy and needs authoring time and reviewer capacity.
Enterprise competitors (Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli) already ship SCORM/LTI and video avatars; the open-source core should not chase enterprise parity.
